scope: One complete known Train document and eight synthetic inputs. Read all inputs and all 18 baseline/rendered POS/tag/dependency/head tables. Inspect the resulting source projections separately. The first six inputs are those from the earlier manual-boundary probe; the additional cases cover an entity and word-internal emphasis, inline code with a link, and literal unclosed markup.

cases.finding: Removing emphasis syntax from the declared text view separates the previously fused noun, dash and main verb. The subject becomes nsubj of the VBD/ROOT main verb, and the accompanying participle attaches to that verb. The noun is now tagged NOUN/NNS; the manual-boundary intervention had tagged it PROPN/NNP. Earlier coordination, free-relative copular and contracted-negation errors remain.

All three now recover the main root and subject, including the single-asterisk case that still failed after manual token splitting. Their complete rendered annotations equal the unformatted control. Formatting markers no longer receive grammatical roles.
cases.remaining_error: The common rendered analysis tags the finite main verb VBN rather than VBD. The earlier manual splitting produced VBD in the strong/underscore variants, so the new view does not improve every field relative to that intervention.

cases.finding: Raw and rendered annotations are identical apart from the declared view identity. The longer control retains its incorrect participle tag; the simple control retains the expected finite root, subject and temporal phrase.

The rendered adjective is available as one token, instead of a token fused with emphasis delimiters and spurious object markers. The embedded-predication representation was read but not independently adjudicated. The entity-containing token and the word crossing emphasis delimiters both correctly lack a contiguous verbatim source projection.

The guide label becomes the object of opening; the raw parse had instead attached URL material as its object. Inline code remains visible to NLP but is protected from a verbatim edit projection. The link label has an exact source span.

The literal asterisk and underscore-containing term survive. The complete annotation matches the raw control, including the inappropriate interjection tag on the term used as a coordinated noun. Literal punctuation is not automatically formatting.

limitations: A selected nine-input development comparison cannot estimate corpus accuracy. This implements an optional Rust text-view adapter, not a replacement for spaCy or a change to existing model inputs. HTML and images remain explicit unsupported constructs; code stays protected text. Refit and evaluate any new representation consistently before using its features or gradients in B.
